info.title: Dispatch HTTP API
info.description: Generated from the /api/v2 rows of the Go route table (the v2<Group>Rows functions of internal/dispatch/api/v2_<group>.go) and the query, body and answer types each row declares, by `envoy-dispatch openapi`. Edit those, never this document: it is committed so a client's types can be rendered from it, and `envoy-dispatch openapi --check` refuses a tree where it is stale. Each operation of a /api/v2 row lists the refusal codes it can answer with their statuses (x-refusal-codes): its row's own and those of every layer the server runs it behind, but the router's origin and host guards in front of every route (ORIGIN_REFUSED, HOST_MISMATCH), the test hooks (SLOW_WRITE_CUT_OFF) and a server built with no store (DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE). components.x-refusal-codes lists every code /api/v2 can answer, once; every object a Go struct answers declares each member it can hold and no other.

get.description: What people wrote that Dispatch delivered to one session, newest first by at, then by id: each ask's current answer (replaced when it changed an earlier answer), each comment at its current body (edited_at when edited; a resolved comment stays), each message at its current body (edited_at when edited), a deleted comment or message in its place with deleted_at and deleted_by and an empty text, and each ask a person declined to answer, once however it arrived, each naming its relation to the session, its author, its words (text, and on declined_your_ask alone dispatch_words, the sentences Dispatch wrote for the asking agent), the ask and its whole question where it has one, whoever asked it, its owner, dispatch:// ref and href. A session owns an ask when it wrote the ask or follows it, and only an owner is told that an ask is its own: answered_your_ask, declined_your_ask and replied_on_your_ask (which outranks mentioned_you) for an owner, answered_an_ask and declined_an_ask for any other session, which reads a reply in an ask's thread by the reason that delivered it. It never lists an agent's or the system's words. from and to window at, RFC3339, from inclusive and to exclusive: from defaults to 72 hours ago, and one older than 7 days or in the future is 400 INVALID_QUERY, as is a to not after from. limit 1 to 200 (default 50) and offset page the window; max_chars (1 to 100000) then stops the page after the item whose words take the running sum past it, counting the UTF-16 units of text and of dispatch_words, while total counts every item in the window. {session_id, from, to, items, total, limit, offset}, to null where the request names none. A session_id that is not a session id is 400 INVALID_SESSION_ID; a session Dispatch holds nothing for answers an empty page. Not an authorization boundary: a person may read any session's list.

get.description: List the files and images of an agent's conversation, oldest first. Each artifact is one row: its own fields (id, issue_key, project, session_id, ref_key, slug, name, kind doc, image or file, primary, role, created_by, created_at), latest_version, the number of its newest version, latest_version_at, when that version was written, and latest_version_size, the bytes it stores (each null for an artifact with no version, and the size null for a version that records none), version_count, how many versions it holds, and a document's approval {state, latest_version, version, by, at, reason, ask_id, ...}; its versions are GET /api/v2/artifacts/{id}/versions. slug=<slug> keeps the one at ref_key agent/<session_id>/<slug>, as dispatch://agent/<session_id>/artifact/<slug> names it; a conversation holds no document, so no file name is matched. limit 1 to 200 (default 50) and offset; {items, total, limit, offset}. A session Dispatch holds no file of answers the empty list; a session_id that is empty or holds /, ?, #, whitespace, a control character or <>"'`[]| is 400 INVALID_SESSION_ID. The list that names no slug is part of the conversation, so it needs the person scope (403 OAUTH_SCOPE_REQUIRED) and admits exactly the callers GET /api/v2/agents/{session_id}/messages admits, as GET /api/v1/agents/{session_id}/artifacts does; the read of one file by its slug needs no more than GET /api/v1/agents/{session_id}/artifacts/{slug} does.

post.description: Upload a file or image to an agent's conversation: ref_key agent/<session_id>/<slug>, addressed dispatch://agent/<session_id>/artifact/<slug>. JSON {name, content?, summary?, actor?, precondition?} stores a markdown document, or multipart with a file part and the fields name, summary, actor and precondition stores the file: a text/markdown file is a document, any other an image only when its bytes are a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, stored under the type its bytes are, and otherwise a file under its declared type. An upload under a name or slug the owner already holds is that artifact's next version. A conversation holds files and images only. To replace a file or a picture, precondition {document} names the latest version's token, which GET /api/v2/artifacts/{id}/versions?sort=-number&limit=1 answers on that version; a replacement naming none is taken unchecked. A stale token is 409 PRECONDITION_FAILED with the token and version that stand; a first upload or a version with no token also refuses a named token. A precondition naming blocks is 400 INVALID_PRECONDITION. Answers 201 {artifact, version}, artifact the artifact's row as it stands once the upload is stored (its own fields, latest_version, latest_version_at, latest_version_size, version_count and a document's approval) and version the version the upload wrote, for a new artifact and for a new version alike. A body that is neither JSON nor multipart is 415 JSON_CONTENT_TYPE, and an empty JSON body 400 INVALID_JSON; 400 ARTIFACT_INPUT (primary given, content beside a file, blank content under an existing document's name, a markdown document, as JSON content or a text/markdown file), ARTIFACT_KIND_MISMATCH, INVALID_ARTIFACT (no name, no file, a new name or key over 2692 bytes), 413 REQUEST_TOO_LARGE past 25 MB or a markdown document past 1 MiB. No event is appended. A caller whose credential proves a session of its own uploads only into that session: any other session_id is 403 SESSION_SCOPE; a session_id that is no session id is 400 INVALID_SESSION_ID.

post.description: Send an issue-less targeted message to a session {body, delivery, in_reply_to?, in_reply_to_block?, connected_only?}, which needs the person scope: delivery is btw, aside or steer, and a reply names a message of this session's conversation in in_reply_to. It is answered 201 once its own attempt has settled. A session the Envoy listener knows and that is not running is a recipient: the listener stores the message and hands it over when that session runs again, and the attempt is recorded queued; one the listener knows nothing about fails the attempt with "no live session <id>". connected_only asks for a session running now and fails the attempt with "the session is stopped", nothing stored, as a person's own Send or Aside whose whole body is one /model or /effort line always does. A repeat under its Idempotency-Key answers the message as it stands, its owed attempt sent first. 400 INVALID_MESSAGE or MESSAGE_INPUT for a message it refuses, the second for an in_reply_to outside this session's conversation among others.

get.description: What changed between two stored versions of one document, version_from=<n>&version_to=<m>: {artifact_id, from, to, decision_only, unchanged, sections, blocks}, both versions read from their stored markdown with every ask block cut out, so the block index's deferred pass is never waited for. Exactly one of three holds: decision_only, true when the two stored texts differ and cut to the same text; unchanged, true when the two differ in nothing any section or block holds (the stored texts are the same, or the cut texts name nothing and are not decision-only); or sections and blocks name at least one item. sections and blocks are empty when decision_only or unchanged is true. sections is each top-level unit whose text differs, that moved, or that one version alone holds: a `##` section by heading and occurrence (the heading's text as a heading anchor reads it, without markdown's syntax and with a line break in it as a line feed; 0 for the first section of that heading, so a `##` heading with no words counts from occurrence 1), and a run of the text outside every `##` section (the title and what stands above the first `##`, or what follows a `#` heading up to the next `##`) under heading "" and occurrence 0 with its place: place before_first_section, or place after_section with after_heading and after_occurrence naming the `##` section directly before the run, in the later version for a changed, added or moved run and in the earlier for a removed one. A `#` or `##` heading that holds a line break, which is stored in setext form with no `#`, cuts the document as any heading of its level does. blocks is each typed block but an ask whose text or any attribute differs, by id and type. Each unit and block is marked changed, added or removed, and a unit whose text is the same is marked moved when its place among the document's top-level units is another: it stands outside one longest common subsequence of the two versions' orders of the units both hold, and of several that long the one kept holds the later version's earliest units, so of two units that swapped places the later version's second is moved. Both versions hold a run when both hold its text at the same place, and then, among the runs left in each version, the n-th run of one text in each is one run in both, so adding or removing one copy of a repeated run moves no other copy's match; a run the other version does not hold pairs with that version's unpaired run at the same place and is marked changed, and a run left unpaired is added or removed. A block is never marked moved. Each list holds the later version's items in its document order, a moved unit where the later version holds it, then what only the earlier holds, in its order. version_from and version_to are both required, each a version number from 1 to 2147483647 (the largest version number the store holds), and version_from below version_to (400 INVALID_QUERY); a version the document does not have is 404 NOT_FOUND, a file or an image 400 NOT_DOCUMENT, and 404 ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND.
